image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a sea lion resting on a rocky surface. The animal is curled up, with its head tucked towards its body. The fur appears wet and coarse, transitioning from dark brown/black on the back to lighter brown on the sides. One foreflipper is visible, tucked under the body, appearing dark and leathery. The external ear flap is faintly visible on the side of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is turned away and partially obscured by the angle and the curling posture; the sagittal crest cannot be clearly verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: External ear pinnae (visible ear flaps) distinguish from true seals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A small, distinct flap-like structure is visible on the side of the head, consistent with the external ear pinnae of a sea lion.
The snout area is out of focus or obscured by the angle; individual whiskers are not resolvable.

The asymmetrical pose prevents verification of overall bilateral symmetry.
